facts.title: Above the bill
facts.text: The Rhinoceros Hornbill has a raised, upturned casque above its bill.

facts.title: Fruit in the canopy
facts.text: Rhinoceros Hornbills eat mostly fruit and often visit fruiting fig trees.

facts.title: A hollow for a nest
facts.text: Rhinoceros Hornbills use tree cavities to nest.

facts.title: Food through a small opening
facts.text: A nesting female Rhinoceros Hornbill closes most of the cavity entrance. The male passes food through the opening.

facts.title: Seeds on the move
facts.text: Fruit-eating hornbills can move seeds away from their parent trees, helping some seeds reach new places to grow.

facts.title: Gunung Mulu limestone
facts.text: The limestone at Gunung Mulu forms caves and the sharp pinnacles above the forest.

facts.title: Roots at the riverbank
facts.text: Streamside roots hold soil together and can reduce bank erosion.

facts.title: Connected habitat
facts.text: When forest is split into patches, some animals find it harder to move between them. Habitat corridors can help.

facts.title: Mangrove wildlife
facts.text: Proboscis monkeys use Sarawak's mangrove forests, where they can feed on mangrove leaves.

facts.title: Share the habitat story
facts.text: Keep directions, recognisable landmarks and precise locations of active nests out of public updates.

facts.title: Report wildlife concerns safely
facts.text: In Sarawak, give the animal space and contact park staff or Sarawak Forestry Corporation for guidance.

facts.title: Food changes behaviour
facts.text: Feeding wildlife can teach animals to approach people for food. Observe them from a distance and take scraps away.

facts.title: A seed above the ground
facts.text: Some strangler figs start on another tree's branches. Their roots grow down towards the ground.

facts.title: Belian
facts.text: Belian is also called Bornean ironwood. Its scientific name is Eusideroxylon zwageri.

facts.title: A red meranti in Borneo
facts.text: Meranti tembaga is one example of a light red meranti that occurs naturally in Borneo.

facts.title: Mengaris
facts.text: Mengaris is one Sabah name for the tall forest tree Koompassia excelsa.

facts.title: Help existing seedlings
facts.text: Forest recovery can include protecting native regrowth already suited to local conditions.

facts.title: Return to count
facts.text: A follow-up survey tells a restoration team how many seedlings survived after planting.

facts.title: Keep mature nesting trees
facts.text: Large mature trees can contain natural hollows that hornbills use. Keeping those trees retains possible nest sites.

facts.title: What a nest box adds
facts.text: A nest box may add a possible nest site. Hornbills still need suitable habitat and reliable food sources.
